Operator: Good day, and welcome to the NexWave Communications Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then 1 on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to NexWave Communications' Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Raj Singh, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Reilly, Chief Network Officer; and other members of our leadership team. Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for the third quarter. We exceeded expectations in several key areas. First, we delivered strong net subscriber additions across residential and business segments, totaling nearly 300,000. Second, ARPU trends showed solid uplift from our pricing discipline and bundling strategies. We are seeing very positive results from our investments in 5G Standalone network, and its impact on enterprise services is significant. Third, our enterprise and B2B growth initiatives posted impressive wins and acceleration. Fourth, our network investments are yielding high returns in coverage and performance. Finally, we are strategically positioning ourselves for continued EBITDA margin expansion through operational efficiencies.

Raj Singh: Thank you, Elena. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $22.5 billion, up 14% year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $9.0 billion, resulting in a margin of 40%. We are maintaining strict cost discipline. Capital expenditures were $7.5 billion, primarily allocated to 5G rollout and fiber expansion. Now, let me dive deeper into some of these highlights, starting with one of our fastest-growing segments: enterprise and B2B services. This area is central to our strategy of diversifying beyond consumer wireless and broadband into high-margin, sticky revenue streams that leverage our world-class 5G Standalone network, extensive fiber backbone, and media delivery expertise. In the third quarter, enterprise and B2B revenue accelerated 28% year-over-year to around $1.9 billion, representing 23% of our total service revenue—up from 18% a year ago. On a constant currency basis, that's even stronger growth at about 30%, driven by robust demand for private networks, edge computing, and our 5G-optimized Unified Communications as a Service platform.

Year-to-date, B2B revenue is pacing at over $5.5 billion, a 26% increase from the prior year, outpacing our consumer segment's growth. Average revenue per user in enterprise climbed 15% to roughly $4,200 monthly, fueled by multi-year contracts with embedded services like AI-powered network slicing and cybersecurity overlays. Churn remains best-in-class at under 1.2% annually, thanks to our 98% service level agreement uptime on our 5G SA core, which now covers 85% of the U.S. footprint and is expanding rapidly in Europe. We're seeing strong secular tailwinds: the global enterprise 5G market is projected to hit $100 billion by 2028, with private 5G networks growing at a 65% compound annual rate. Post-pandemic hybrid work has supercharged demand for low-latency SD-WAN and our NexWave Edge platform, which integrates with hyperscalers like AWS Outposts and Microsoft Azure Edge Zones. In media, our Content Delivery Network business—powered by our 1.2 million miles of subsea and terrestrial fiber—handled 45% more enterprise traffic quarter-over-quarter, supporting live sports streaming and AR/VR experiences for clients like regional sports leagues similar to those partnered with Sinclair Broadcast Group.

Regionally, North America, which accounts for 65% of B2B revenue, was up 32% year-over-year, driven by U.S. manufacturing reshoring, with our fiber-to-the-edge deployments in Rust Belt states enabling ultra-reliable private 5G for Industry 4.0 applications. Europe grew 22% despite regulatory headwinds on spectrum auctions, as we've capitalized on the EU's Gigabit Society targets, winning deals in Germany and the UK. APAC saw explosive 45% year-over-year expansion via our Singapore hub, targeting smart cities and gaming media in Japan and Australia. EBITDA margins in this segment expanded 450 basis points to 42%, reflecting scale in our software-defined networking stack and reduced capex intensity—now at 18% of revenue versus 25% last year—as we shift to virtualized RAN partnerships with Nokia and Ericsson.

Key wins from the quarter highlight this momentum. We closed a $750 million, five-year private 5G network deal for a major U.S. automotive giant—think along the lines of Ford or GM—deployed across 12 manufacturing plants in Michigan and Ohio, delivering 10 Gbps symmetrical speeds with ultra-reliable low-latency communications for robotic assembly lines and automated guided vehicles. We've bundled our NexWave AI Orchestrator for predictive maintenance, projecting $150 million in upsell from IoT sensor fleets over the contract life. This deal contributed over $120 million to quarterly revenue and validates our leadership in the automotive vertical, where we're now number two behind AT&T FirstNet in enterprise 5G share.

Another standout was a $450 million multi-region SD-WAN and edge contract with a global retailer similar to Walmart, a four-year renewal-plus-expansion covering 4,500 stores across the U.S. and Canada. Our SD-WAN fabric, integrated with VMware SASE, reduced their WAN costs by 35% while enabling real-time inventory AI via edge inference on our 5G multi-access edge computing nodes. This includes our first major Canadian deployment post-Rogers merger synergies, tapping into the $2.5 billion Canadian enterprise connectivity market.

We also secured a $320 million media enterprise deal with a European broadcaster consortium inspired by BBC or RTE partnerships, a three-year agreement to revamp their hybrid cloud CDN for 4K and 8K over-the-top delivery and interactive esports. Leveraging our media heritage—like powering NBA League Pass streams—we've deployed 200 Gbps lambda services over our pan-European fiber ring, growing our media B2B share by 15% in EMEA, with embedded ad-tech analytics adding $50 million in high-margin annual recurring revenue.

In APAC, a $200 million smart city IoT platform for a Singapore government-linked entity marked our first sovereign-grade private 5G deployment in Southeast Asia, integrating with their Smart Nation initiative, including narrowband IoT for 500,000 street sensors yielding 99.999% reliability—a beachhead for a $1 billion pipeline in ASEAN amid Huawei restrictions. Smaller but strategic wins totaled $150 million, including a $60 million UCaaS rollout for a Fortune 100 financial services firm migrating 150,000 seats to our Webex-competitive platform with 5G fallback, and $40 million in vRAN upgrades for a Japanese telco partner aligning with their Open RAN push.

These wins prove our 5G Media Fusion strategy: converging telecom infrastructure with media workloads for differentiated B2B value. We're investing $500 million in fiscal 2025 capex for 2,000 additional MEC sites, targeting latency under 5 milliseconds for AR/VR enterprise apps, like remote surgery pilots with Mayo Clinic analogs. Partnerships like our AWS co-sell motion have unlocked 30% of our pipeline, while our Ericsson vRAN joint venture reduces opex by 25%. Supply chain risks for mmWave radios persist, but we've derisked via domestic manufacturing under CHIPS Act incentives. Competitively, we're gaining share from T-Mobile Enterprise and Vodafone Business, with win rates up to 42%. Looking ahead, we guide Q4 B2B revenue at $1.9 to $2.0 billion, 27-30% year-over-year growth, with full-year at $7.5 to $7.8 billion. Our $10 billion B2B backlog—up 35% year-over-year—gives 95% visibility into 2025 revenue, driving 60% of incremental EBITDA growth.

Shifting to ARPU trends and the impact of our pricing and bundling strategies, which are key levers for sustainable revenue growth. Our consolidated blended ARPU came in at $58.42 for the quarter, a robust 4.8% year-over-year increase, or plus $2.68. This is the strongest quarterly uplift since late 2021, surpassing our guidance. By segment, postpaid mobile ARPU rose to $52.17, up 5.2% or plus $2.58, fixed broadband at $76.34, up 3.9% or plus $2.87, and emerging video and media services at $14.62 per household, surging 12.1% or plus $1.58, driven by streaming bundles.

These results stem from disciplined pricing actions and innovative bundling amid moderating churn. We've implemented targeted price increases averaging 4-6% on select unlimited plans and fiber tiers, aligned with 3.2% CPI in core U.S. markets. Our Unlimited Max 5G plan saw a $5 monthly hike to $85, with softer $3 adjustments for legacy customers, contributing 2.8 points to ARPU growth, with net adds stable and churn at 0.92%. In Europe, annual renewals lifted ARPU 3.1% to €48.20 equivalent, bolstered by MVNO partnerships like Vodafone in the UK. In Latin America, via expansions like Oi Fibra, we optimized mix for 6.7% uplift to $18.40.

Bundling via our NexWave Stack platform now covers 68% of 45 million postpaid subscribers. Mobile-plus-broadband double-plays generated $3.20 incremental ARPU at 42% penetration, priced at $129.99 for 1Gig fiber plus unlimited 5G. Triple and quad-plays with NexWave Stream—exclusive FAST channels and Paramount+, Peacock content—added $4.50 per household, with VoxUltimate quad at $149.99 driving 18% video ARPU growth and 2.1 million net adds via NBA League Pass deals. U.S. Northeast and California saw plus 6.2% ARPU from FTTH overbuilds; APAC joint ventures yielded plus 9.4% to SGD 62 equivalent.

Network investments amplify this: 85% 5G Ultra Wideband footprint enables $8 monthly premiums for mmWave; 3 million new GPON ports support gigabit speeds. Edge partnerships with AWS cut video buffering 40%, boosting NPS to 72. We expect 4-5% YoY ARPU through 2024, targeting 75% bundling penetration, with 98% retention from loyalty programs and wholesale 5G slicing for B2B upside.

Next, on net subscriber additions by segment. We delivered total net adds of 295,000 across residential and business, up 12% year-over-year and accelerating from Q2. Residential posted 250,000 broadband and mobility adds, up 15% from last year: 180,000 in FTTH/gigabit (72%), 45,000 FWA in suburbs, and 125,000 postpaid mobile from 5G upgrades and family bundles with NexWave Stream edge caching for 4K. Churn at 0.85% monthly, down 10 basis points, via AI retention tools. U.S. Northeast/Southeast added 140,000, up 20%, from $2.5 billion FTTH partnerships; Latin America 65,000 via Claro Brasil; Europe 45,000 despite pressures. Residential ARPU up 3% to $68 from 5G Home Internet (1.2 million subs, 40% growth) and 25% Stream penetration.

Business achieved 45,000 net adds, up 25% year-over-year: 12,000 SMB from NovaBiz Fiber Connect targeting 100,000 locations, 18,000 enterprise managed services like Verizon-AWS hybrid cloud. Ethernet/fiber 22,000, wireless/IoT 15,000; churn 0.45%. North America 28,000 (62%), from Northern Virginia dark fiber; APAC 10,000 smart manufacturing; EMEA 7,000. Our Fiber First, 5G Everywhere approach has 15 million FTTH homes at 35% take rates, 2 million FWA pipeline. Full-year on track for 1.1 million adds.

Regarding EBITDA margin guidance, Q3 hit 40.1% or $2.85 billion on $14.2 billion revenue—up 220 basis points year-over-year. For Q4 2024, we guide 41.5% to 42.5%, or $3.0 to $3.1 billion on $14.5 to $14.7 billion revenue. Tailwinds: $250 million opex savings from Project Horizon zero-based budgeting, AI chatbots cutting handle times 25%; 5G SA in 80% top MSAs boosting efficiency to 1.2 TB per cell; StreamForge integration adding $150 million uplift, churn to 4.2%. North America at 43.2%, Europe 38.5%, Latin America 32.1%. For full-year 2025, raising to 42% to 44%, or $12.2 to $12.6 billion on $29.0 to $29.5 billion revenue. Drivers: capex to $7.5-8.0 billion (26% of revenue), wireless 5-6% growth, media 15%; bolt-on fiber M&A. Risks: spectrum pricing, content inflation; upsides: FWA, Dish assets.

Finally, capital expenditure guidance for network investments. Total FY2025 capex guided at $24 to $26 billion, up 5-8%, targeting $8-10 billion FCF. Network-specific: $20 to $22 billion, 82-85% of total, up 10%. Wireless $13-14 billion: 1,200 new small cells, 85% SA coverage, $5.5 billion Open RAN with Nokia/Ericsson/Rakuten for 15-20% opex cuts; 70% North America, 20% Europe. Wireline $4.5-5 billion: FTTH to 15 million locations, 50 million passings, 45% take rates, $1.2 billion rural middle-mile. Media/edge $2.5-3 billion: edge DCs, AWS Outposts for 10 Tbps 8K, vRAN for $1.2 billion Fortune 500 deals. This drives ARPU uplifts, 6G pilots by Q4 2025. Risks mitigated via procurement, MSAs.

Tom Reilly: Thank you, Raj. I would like to provide an update on our network performance. We have made significant progress in expanding our 5G coverage to 90% of our U.S. footprint, with standalone core now live in key markets. Our network reliability metrics continue to improve, averaging 99.999% uptime, and we are seeing increased data usage across our customer base, up 25% year-over-year. We are also actively working on enhancing our cybersecurity infrastructure with AI-driven threat detection. Our team's dedication to edge computing and fiber densification has been instrumental in achieving these results, supporting both consumer streaming and enterprise private networks.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, please press star then 1. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you discuss the competitive landscape and your strategy for retaining market share in enterprise 5G services?

Elena Vasquez: Certainly, John. The enterprise 5G space is heating up with players like T-Mobile and Verizon pushing hard, but our differentiated 5G Media Fusion approach—combining private networks, edge computing, and media CDN—gives us an edge. We've gained share through wins like the $750 million automotive deal and 42% win rates, leveraging partnerships with AWS and Ericsson. We'll continue investing in MEC sites and vRAN to maintain leadership, targeting that $100 billion market by 2028.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. What are your expectations for subscriber growth in the next quarter, and how will that impact EBITDA margins?

Raj Singh: We anticipate around 320,000 net adds in Q4, with residential steady at 260,000 from FWA and fiber, business accelerating to 60,000 on SD-WAN demand. This, combined with 4% ARPU growth and opex savings, will drive Q4 margins to 41.5-42.5%, on track for 42-44% in 2025 as higher-margin B2B mix expands.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Lopez with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Lopez: Can you provide an update on your fiber deployment plans and the expected ROI on those investments?

Tom Reilly: Absolutely, Mike. We're on pace to pass 15 million new FTTH locations in 2025 with $4.5-5 billion allocated, achieving 45% take rates in greenfields via bundles with NexWave Stream. ROI is tracking at 35% on incremental capex, accelerated by RDOF/BEAD subsidies and symmetric 2Gbps speeds reducing churn. Partnerships for middle-mile dark fiber ensure payback within 24-36 months, rivaling AT&T's builds.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Elena, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Elena Vasquez: Thank you. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain confident in our ability to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value. Thank you for your time and interest in NexWave Communications.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
